mechanism: Loop diuretic torsemide increases renal potassium and sodium loss, while ACE inhibitor ramipril increases potassium retention, creating opposing effects on electrolytes and blood pressure; combined use increases risk of hyperkalemia, hypokalemia, and acute renal dysfunction.
action: Monitor serum potassium, creatinine, and blood pressure regularly; adjust doses based on renal function and electrolytes; counsel patient on dietary potassium intake.
